standard: The model can speak. It does not get the answer.
evidence: Gemini reads a player's question, plays the wolf, and voices both characters. The deterministic game engine keeps the rune secret and decides every claim.

standard: A model can observe without getting to diagnose.
evidence: Gemma runs on the phone. Audio is discarded after inference, the three lens reads stay visible, and patterns cite the entries that earned them.

standard: A match only counts once every toxic look-alike loses.
evidence: BioCLIP 2.5 Mobile and TinyCLIP ViT-8M/16 Text-3M check every photo on the phone — a find has to beat every toxic plant nearby, three frames running. None of the 267 toxic test photos have passed. Gemma 4 26B A4B wrote the hints on a laptop and never made it into the app.

standard: Every country keeps its own aircraft register. The feed ships one schema and drops the home addresses.
evidence: Civil-aviation registers map into one SQLite file in Cloudflare R2, with the source license and attribution kept on every row. An unchanged register doesn't redeploy — and an ambiguous tail number fails the build.

standard: A model may write a note. It does not get a general database connection.
evidence: Seven narrow tools, Zod validation before Postgres, revision history on every write, and a batch response that says exactly which cards failed.

standard: AI attribution belongs in the commit, not the postmortem.
evidence: The Node and Python linters reject a commit without an attribution footer and a human sign-off. The record is enforced where the work enters history.

standard: Natural language still has to respect the read boundary.
evidence: Cortex Analyst writes the SQL, so the guard sits between it and the warehouse: SELECT-only and single-statement, run under a least-privilege read-only role, with a 10-second statement timeout and a 500-row ceiling.

standard: Mute the audio and turn off the shaders — the memoir still reads straight through.
evidence: A vanilla JavaScript scene engine keeps Canvas 2D, PixiJS shaders, GSAP timelines, and Howler.js audio in step. The canvas is hidden from screen readers; the DOM carries the whole story.
